text:
Anita: Quick PSA — I ran a focused NCCL/channel sweep on the 8xA100 cluster this morning to try to reduce all‑reduce tail latency for tensor+pipeline parallel runs. posting raw notes + a couple of config snippets.

Matt: Awesome, interested in numbers. did you use LL or LL128 by default?

Anita: Started with proto=LL and algo=Ring baseline. Then tried proto=LL128 + channels=4 and proto=LL + channels=8. Also toggled NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD and NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS.

Jeff: What workload? long sequence generation or short microbatches?

Anita: Mixed. Primary test is gated token generation (seq_len 2048, microbatch 1-2 tokens). Also ran a batched decode workload (mb=16) to compare.

Sara: Did you profile where the time goes? allreduce / compute / kernel launch?

Anita: Yes — used Nsight + our perf harness. Summary (median per-step):
- baseline (Ring, proto=LL, channels=1): allreduce 3.2ms, compute 8.6ms, step 12.0ms
- LL128 + channels=4: allreduce 1.05ms, compute 8.9ms, step 10.4ms (network wins, small cpu overhead)
- proto=LL + channels=8: allreduce 0.9ms, compute 9.1ms, step 10.5ms
- For microbatch=1 (KV-heavy tiny tensors): baseline allreduce 4.8ms, LL128 channels=4 -> 1.8ms but added serialization overhead for small fragments in our runtime -> step 11.2ms

perf-bot: Quick summary: LL128 reduces raw allreduce time for large contiguous tensors. Small fragmented tensors still pay high per-call cost unless fused.

Matt: Interesting. So LL128 helps bulk, but microbatches + many tiny KV shards still expensive. Any kernel-level changes to fuse KV shards?

Anita: That's the heart of it. Our current kernel selection sometimes emits separate allreduces for each KV shard because sizes are below the fuse threshold. Two avenues:
1) Improve runtime fusion: group small tensors by data type + dtype+device into a single fused tensor before NCCL ops.
2) Prefer LL or Tree proto for tiny fused calls because LL128 has more per-channel state assumptions that don't amortize for tiny sizes.

Jeff: Can you paste the env/config variants you tested?

Anita: Sure — this is exactly what I iterated with:

```
# baseline
export NCCL_ALGO=Ring
export NCCL_PROTO=LL
export NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=1
export NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0

# tuned
export NCCL_ALGO=Tree
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
export NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=4
export NCCL_NTHREADS=16
export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL
# optional: try enabling hierarchical if available
export NCCL_HIERARCHICAL=1
```

Anita: Note: Tree+LL128 gave best numbers on medium tensors; Ring+LL sometimes outperformed for a bunch of tiny allreduces because of lower setup cost per call.

Sara: Did you try merging K/V cache allreduces across layers? like fold across attention heads to reduce number of operations?

Anita: I tried a quick POC where we concat the KV shards along an extra dim per-device before allreduce. That reduced call count by ~60% and improved microbatch latency by ~1.5ms on average. But it increased peak GPU memory by ~2-3% because of the temporary buffer. Tradeoff seems worthwhile at our memory headroom.

Matt: Anything actionable for the runtime ASAP?

Anita: Yes — proposed short plan:
- small change: lower fuse threshold to 8KB and enable type+device grouping (config flag runtime.kv_fuse_bytes=8192). This nets ~30% fewer NCCL calls in the microbatch path.
- medium change: add a proto hint per-fused-op: if fused_size > 64KB prefer LL128 + channels=4, else prefer Tree+LL.
- long change: implement a single-shot fused allreduce kernel for tiny KV shards (avoid NCCL for tensors < 2KB) — risky but could pay off.

Jeff: For the medium change, do we have safe defaults to avoid regressions on other customers?

Anita: Yes. Default runtime: kv_fuse_bytes=16KB, nnccl_proto_hint=auto. We gate the more aggressive fuse on canary and use canary group in Dedicated clusters.

perf-bot: Canary config baked: runtime.kv_fuse_bytes=8192, nnccl_min_channels=4, prefer_proto=LL128_for_fused_large.

Sara: Any profiling outputs you can attach? stack traces or flame graphs?

Anita: Dropped a small flame snapshot to the bench bucket, link in thread: https://bench.internal/redwood/nccl-sweep/1744101234/profile.html (internal). Highlights:
- The long tail was dominated by hundreds of 0.1-0.5ms NCCL calls.
- Kernel selection sometimes picked small-element kernels that launched extra syncs. We need to prefer fused kernel paths for small contiguous KV layout.

Matt: Good. I'll add a canary rollout ticket and tag infra to monitor p99. x-signal?

Anita: Ticket created: RDW-3581 — canary rollout + perf alerts. I'll attach the config diff.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy for eng-runtime/canary at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z (ID: cd-1744).

Jeff: One more micro-optimization: set NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=131072 for large models to force LL128 on >128KB buffers, but allow LL for tiny ones. Worth trying in canary variant.

Anita: Yup that's in the patch. Also adding a small runtime metric: n_ncsll_calls and fused_bytes to trace per-step. That will help evaluate fusion benefit.

Matt: Perfect. If canary looks good, let's roll to Dedicated next week. Great work! :rocket: 

Sara: :thumbsup: I'll run a couple more long-seq tests overnight and post numbers in the morning.

Anita: Thanks all — follow up tomorrow with canary numbers.
